name: Streetwear
region: Los Angeles, New York and Tokyo
summary: The casual dress that grew from surf, skate, hip-hop and sport clubs from 1980. It has the graphic T-shirt, the hoodie, the baggy jean, the nylon trouser and the cap, sold in small drops.

philosophy.core_thesis: Dress comes from the street and the club: the wearer joins a group by a plain, comfortable garment that carries a mark.
design_principles: Cut the T-shirt and the hoodie boxy and 5 to 10 cm wider than the body.
Print a mark, a name or a graphic on the chest in one to four flat colours by screen print.
Choose heavy cotton jersey of 200 to 300 g/m² and brushed-back loopback terry for the hoodie.
Cut the jean or the trouser wide and straight, and let the hem break on the shoe.
Add one sport or work element: a nylon panel, a zip pocket or a drawcord.
Release the piece in a small run, so that few people own it.
Pair the garment with a cap and a sneaker.
anti_patterns: Sharp tailoring and a pressed crease
Fine, fragile cloth that cannot be washed

silhouette.shape: A loose, boxy rectangle on top with a wide, straight leg, finished by a cap and a thick-soled shoe.
silhouette.line: A dropped shoulder, a hem at the hip, and a trouser hem that rests on the shoe.
silhouette.fit: Loose and comfortable; the garment hangs free of the body and is easy to move in.
silhouette.proportion: T-shirt 5 to 10 cm wider than the chest. Hoodie hem at the hip. Jean leg 22 to 26 cm at the hem. Cap crown 10 cm.
rules: Drop the shoulder seam 4 to 8 cm below the natural line.
Keep the hoodie hem and cuff in a rib knit.
Cut the jean or trouser wide and full from the hip.
Place the mark on the chest or the back, at 10 to 25 cm in width.
Add a cap or a beanie and a sneaker.

fabrics.rule: Choose a hard-wearing, washable cloth from work and sport: heavy cotton jersey, loopback terry, denim, canvas and nylon.

methods: boxy cut with a dropped shoulder
construction.closures: A drawcord, a kangaroo pocket, a zip or a snap; trousers with an elastic or drawcord waist.
construction.details: A woven label, a printed back graphic, a kangaroo pocket, a ribbed collar and a cap with a flat brim.

surface.pattern: A logo, a name or a graphic on the chest or the back; a camouflage or a plain block of colour.
surface.gloss: Cotton at 2–8 GU; nylon at 20–50 GU; a print at 10–40 GU.
surface.wear: The style takes wear well: a washed, faded and softened piece is liked, but a new drop is also prized.

palette.strategy: A base of black, white and grey with one or two strong accent colours taken from a team or a skate brand.

processes: cut and sew in small runs
making.scale: Small independent runs and limited drops; larger brands and sport firms make the same pieces in mass runs.
making.signs: A woven neck label, a printed hang tag, and a heavy knit with a clean rib.

pieces.form: Boxy cotton T-shirt with a chest graphic
Heavy hooded sweatshirt with a kangaroo pocket
Wide, straight jeans with a stonewashed face
Wide nylon track trouser with a drawcord
Heavy canvas work overshirt with a patch

canonical_works.work: Signature T-shirt with a hand-written mark

emotion.target_response: A feeling of belonging and ease: the viewer sees a relaxed, tough look that signals the wearer's group.

use_cases: a casual clothing line and drop
a costume brief for a youth film
a study note on subculture and brands
avoid_when: the brief wants formal or tailored dress
the brief wants a quiet, luxury, no-logo look
the brief wants a historic costume

modifiers.how: Remove the graphic, use a fine knit and a plain cut, and keep the loose shape.
Strip the print and the logo, and cut the same shapes in plain nylon and wool.
